- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to adjust downward; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% of prior peak if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early days (1–7) and underestimates late days (15–30); apply upward bias to later days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.00 for 3+ consecutive days), model underestimates true price; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
